#' LIBRARIES 

```{r}
library(multiverse)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(lmerTest)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(broom)
library(lme4)
library(knitr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(betareg)
library(flexmix)
library(modeltools)
library(statmod)
library(stats)
```

```{r}
raw_data = read_csv("data/edge1.1.csv")
game = multiverse()


particip_data_duplicates = raw_data %>%  
  dplyr::select(!Order:Number.Characters) %>% 
  group_by(ThreadId, Id) %>%  
  summarize(across(Type:ContributionsbyAuthor,  ~ paste(unique(.x), collapse = "; "))) 
        
 particip_data_filt = particip_data_duplicates %>% 
  filter(if_any(Type:ContributionsbyAuthor, ~ grepl(";", .x)))


 
 #Slight issue --> there are within participant-changes in the variables indicating status --> correction: 
status_rec = raw_data %>% 
  group_by(Id) %>% 
  arrange(Year, .by_group = TRUE) %>% 
  summarise(across(c(AcademicHierarchyStrict, PhD_Institution_SR_Bin, Workplace_SR_Bin,
                     PhD_Institution_US_IR_Bin, Workplace_US_IR_Bin, Discipline, Years_from_PhD), last),
            .groups = "drop")

raw_data = raw_data %>% 
  select(!c(AcademicHierarchyStrict, PhD_Institution_SR_Bin, Workplace_SR_Bin,
            PhD_Institution_US_IR_Bin, Workplace_US_IR_Bin, Discipline, Years_from_PhD)) %>%    # remove the varying versions
  left_join(status_rec, by = "Id")
# This will be joined to the df in the multiverse accordingly
 
raw_data = anti_join(raw_data, particip_data_filt,  by = c("ThreadId", "Id"))

mw_df = raw_data %>%  
  group_by(Id, ThreadId) %>%  
  summarise(words_in_conv = sum(WC), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  group_by(Id) %>%  
  summarise(mean_words = mean(words_in_conv))


 
raw_data = raw_data %>%  
  mutate(percent_by_author = ContributionsbyAuthor/DebateSize, .after = ContributionsbyAuthor) |>
  mutate(AcademicHierarchyStrict = factor(AcademicHierarchyStrict, levels = 1:6, ordered = TRUE), 
         PhD_Institution_SR_Bin = factor(PhD_Institution_SR_Bin, 1:7, ordered = TRUE), 
         Workplace_SR_Bin = factor(Workplace_SR_Bin, 1:6, ordered = TRUE),
         PhD_Institution_US_IR_Bin = factor(PhD_Institution_US_IR_Bin, levels = 1:7, ordered  = TRUE),
         Workplace_US_IR_Bin = factor(Workplace_US_IR_Bin, levels = 1:10, ordered = TRUE)) |> 
  dplyr::select(!c(Order:Number.Characters), WC) %>%  
  dplyr::select(!c(dummy_Natural.Sciences:dummy_Divinity))

raw_data = left_join(raw_data, mw_df, by = "Id")
raw_data <- raw_data %>%  
  mutate(.row = row_number()) # required, so as not to break the summarise down the line --> the group_by(null) could still work but that would break the summarise later --> with this approach, the reference for grouping is basically one row - which keeps the original structure and the summarise block does not have to be modified 

 
```

#' ===================================================================
#' NODE 1: collapsing 
#' @params: (parameters(game)): 
#' $level[[1]]: participant, $level[[2]]: conversation

```{multiverse default-m-1, inside = game}
data_st1 = raw_data %>% 
  group_by(across(branch(level,
    "participant"              ~ Id,
    "conversation_participant" ~ c(Id, ThreadId),
    "post"                     ~ .row))) %>% 
  select(branch(level,
    "participant"              ~ c(
      Id, Id_num, Name, Male, Female, Job_Title, Job_Title_S, UniqueContributors,
      Workplace, HavePhD, PhD_Field, AuthorAndCommenter, PhD_Institution, PhD_Institution_SR, 
      PhD_Institution_US_IR, Total_Citations, H_Index, i10_Index, ContributionsbyAuthor, percent_by_author, 
      AcademicHierarchyStrict, PhD_Institution_SR_Bin, Workplace_SR_Bin, PhD_Institution_US_IR_Bin, 
      Workplace_US_IR_Bin, Discipline, Years_from_PhD, WC, mean_words),
    "conversation_participant" ~ everything(),
    "post"                     ~ everything())) %>% 
  summarise(branch(level,
    "participant"              ~ across(Id_num:mean_words, first),
    "conversation_participant" ~ across(everything(), first),
    "post"                     ~ across(everything(), first)),
    .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
multiverse::parameters(game)
```


#' ===================================================================
#' NODE 2: Selecting relevant variables (for analysis)

```{multiverse default-m-2, inside = game}
data_st1 <- data_st1 %>% 
  mutate(Gender = case_when(Female == 1 ~ "Female",
                            Male == 1 ~ "Male", 
                            Female == NA ~ "Non-binary/Prefer not to say")) # gender variable - female male is not usable in this sense 

data_st2 = data_st1 %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    any_of(c("Id", "ThreadId", ".row")),   # ID keys present at this level
    all_of(c(
      branch(dependent_variable,
        "mean_words"            %when% (level == "participant")              ~ "mean_words",
        "ContributionsbyAuthor" %when% (level == "conversation_participant") ~ "ContributionsbyAuthor",
        "percent_by_author"     %when% (level == "conversation_participant") ~ "percent_by_author",
        "WC"                    %when% (level == "post")                     ~ "WC"),

      # ---- Primary predictor -
      "AcademicHierarchyStrict",
      
       # ---- Needed for the filter in the next node
      "UniqueContributors",

      # ---- Secondary predictors --> instead of typing out 128 fckn universes --> much more flexible approach --> this can be refined on the website
      branch(include_H_Index,
        "yes" ~ "H_Index",
        "no"  ~ NULL),

      branch(include_Total_Citations,
        "yes" ~ "Total_Citations",
        "no"  ~ NULL),

      branch(include_Workplace_US_IR_Bin,
        "yes" ~ "Workplace_US_IR_Bin",
        "no"  ~ NULL),

      branch(include_Workplace_SR_Bin,
        "yes" ~ "Workplace_SR_Bin",
        "no"  ~ NULL), 
      
      # -----------------------------------------------------------
      # Other potential mediators - Bogi <- "Jöttömre öt nap múltán számítsatok. Pirkadatkor, kelet felől."
      # should be a for loop: all decisions can be mixed. only phd variables should be conditional. 
      # if: include havephd, then -> include yearsfromphd? 
      #                           -> include PhD_Institution_SR_Bin? 
      # include Job_title? 
      # include male/female? 
      
      branch(include_Job_Title, 
             "yes" ~ "Job_Title_S", 
             "no" ~ NULL),
      
      branch(include_Gender, 
             "yes" ~ "Gender", 
             "no" ~ NULL), 
    
      branch(include_havephd, 
             "yes" ~ c("HavePhD", 
                       branch(include_PhD_Institution_SR_Bin, 
                            "yes" ~ "PhD_Institution_SR_Bin",
                            "no"  ~ NULL), 
                       branch(include_Years_from_PhD, 
                              "yes" ~ "Years_from_PhD",
                              "no"  ~ NULL)),
             "no" ~ NULL)
    )))

```

```{r}
multiverse::execute_multiverse(game)
```

#' ===================================================================
#' NODE 3.1: DATA FILTERING: NA filtering
#' @param: AcademicHierarchyStrict

```{multiverse default-m-3, inside = game}
data_st3 <- data_st2 %>% 
  filter(branch(na_filtered, 
                "yes" ~ !(is.na(AcademicHierarchyStrict)), 
                "no" ~ AcademicHierarchyStrict == AcademicHierarchyStrict))
```

```{r}
multiverse::execute_multiverse(game)
```

#' ===================================================================
#' NODE 3.2: DATA FILTERING: Number of participants
#' @nodes: no filter, or: UniqueContributors > mean(UniqueContributors)-sd(UniqueContributors)

```{multiverse default-m-4, inside = game}
data_st4 <- data_st3 %>% 
  filter(branch(uniquecontributors_filter, 
                "no" ~ TRUE, 
                "yes" ~ UniqueContributors > (mean(UniqueContributors, na.rm = TRUE) - sd(UniqueContributors, na.rm = TRUE))))
```

```{r}
multiverse::execute_multiverse(game)
```
